html:
A family of Marwari Jain bankers based at Murshidabad, the capital of the Nawabs of Bengal, who were the most powerful financiers in 18th century India. "Jagat Seth", meaning banker of the world, was a title the Mughal emperor granted to the head of the house in 1723.

The family rose with Manikchand, who followed the governor Murshid Quli Khan to Murshidabad. They collected and remitted Bengal's land revenue, ran the mint, changed money and lent to Nawabs, Mughal officials and European companies. Their reach is often compared to that of the Rothschilds in Europe.

In 1757 the banker Mahtab Chand joined the plot against the Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah, helping Robert Clive and Mir Jafar win the Battle of Plassey. It was a fatal bargain. In 1763 the Nawab Mir Qasim had Mahtab Chand and his cousin killed, and as the East India Company took over Bengal's finances, the house lost its role and slowly declined.
